chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abdul Kareem ibn Amr, from Saeed al-A'raj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
There is no Tamattu' (Hajj al-Tamattu') for the people of Sarif, nor for the people of Marr, nor for the people of Mecca.
That is for him whose family is not present in the Sacred Mosque.

key_terms.أَهْلِ سَرِفٍ: People of Sarif (a specific location near Mecca)
key_terms.أَهْلِ مَرٍّ: People of Marr (a specific location near Mecca)
key_terms.مُتْعَةٌ: Tamattu' (a type of Hajj where one performs Umrah first, then Hajj)

ai.seo_question: Do residents of Mecca perform Hajj al-Tamattu'?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies that the permission for Hajj al-Tamattu' in Surah Al-Baqarah is specifically for those whose families reside outside the Sacred Mosque, thereby excluding permanent residents of Mecca who perform Hajj al-Qiran or al-Ifrad. This ruling is central to Shia jurisprudence, distinguishing between the obligations of locals (Ahl al-Makkah) and pilgrims from other regions, and is often discussed in contrast to Sunni views which may apply Tamattu' more broadly.
